decisions.rationale: In armsInterventionsModule and eligibilityCriteria, all participants receive continuing stable-dose pioglitazone and optional continuing stable-dose metformin ("Metformin, if given to be continued at stable dose (at least 1.5 gram per day) up to the end of treatment."), which briefSummary states verbatim as "pioglitazone with or without metformin". Reading 2's "metformin or pioglitazone" comes from a pre-screening exclusion clause ("other than metformin or pioglitazone ... within 3 months prior to the time of screening") and inaccurately implies metformin monotherapy without pioglitazone was an option.

decisions.rationale: outcomeMeasures[0].populationDescription names "Intent to Treat" and explicitly states a measurement/lab-availability exclusion condition ("Some participants may not have had lab results for this specific analysis and therefore excluded."). Under Coding Sheet Rule 4, an Intent-to-Treat population modified by a stated assessment/lab-result condition (rather than bare undefined ITT or strictly all randomised participants with no measurement requirement) is classified as "modified_intention_to_treat_with_stated_condition".

decisions.rationale: Under Rule 4, `all_randomised_and_treated` applies only when an ITT population is defined strictly as all randomised participants who received >=1 dose of study medication with no baseline/post-baseline measurement requirement. Here, `outcomeMeasures[0].populationDescription` states that the ITT Population consisted of all randomized subjects who received at least one injection of study medication and that missing data up to Week 24 were imputed via LOCF only for subjects who had data for at least one scheduled visit (including Early Termination) subsequent to the baseline measurement. For this Week 24 minus Baseline change measure, inclusion in the analysed population (126 and 116 in `outcomeMeasures[0].denoms[0]`, versus 129 and 123 in the `Intent to Treat (ITT)` participant-flow milestone) requires randomized + >=1 dose plus a stated post-baseline scheduled visit data condition, matching `modified_intention_to_treat_with_stated_condition` (`reading_2`).

comparator_class_quotes.text: Participants received albiglutide 30 milligrams (mg) once weekly subcutaneously from Baseline until Week 52, with optional up-titration to 50 mg if additional glycemic control was required. Albiglutide was injected subcutaneously into the abdomen, on alternating right and left sides of the body. Participants also received sitagliptin matching placebo once daily orally.

received a sitagliptin 100 mg overcoated tablet once daily orally from Baseline until Week 52. The dose of sitagliptin was adjusted in a range of 25-100 mg based on the participant's severity of renal impairment using the modification of diet in renal disease (MDRD) formula. Participants also received albiglutide matching placebo once weekly subcutaneously from Baseline until Week 52.

r1_quotes.text: Participants received albiglutide 30 milligrams (mg) once weekly subcutaneously from Baseline until Week 52, with optional up-titration to 50 mg if additional glycemic control was required. Albiglutide was injected subcutaneously into the abdomen, on alternating right and left sides of the body. Participants also received sitagliptin matching placebo once daily orally.

received a sitagliptin 100 mg overcoated tablet once daily orally from Baseline until Week 52. The dose of sitagliptin was adjusted in a range of 25-100 mg based on the participant's severity of renal impairment using the modification of diet in renal disease (MDRD) formula. Participants also received albiglutide matching placebo once weekly subcutaneously from Baseline until Week 52.

deciding_quotes.text: SUPERIORITY_OR_OTHER

Assuming a common standard deviation of 1.2%, an effective sample size of 400 would provide at least 90% power to detect a statistically significant treatment difference of -0.5% (ranolazine vs. placebo) for the reduction of HbA1c from baseline at Week 24 based on a 2-sided alpha of 0.05 and 1:1 randomization.

P-value is from a mixed-effect model including terms for baseline HbA1c value, prior antihyperglycemia therapy, treatment group, visit week, and treatment by visit week interaction. Unstructured covariance matrix was used.
The estimation (LSM) is of the placebo-corrected change from baseline.
The average (mean) change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24 was analyzed.

decisions.rationale: `nonInferiorityType` is `SUPERIORITY_OR_OTHER`, and `nonInferiorityComment`, `statisticalComment`, and `otherAnalysisDescription` are absent. Across `groupDescription`, `pValueComment`, `estimateComment`, and measure `description`, `groupDescription` gives only the sample-size power calculation for an assumed alternative-hypothesis treatment difference of -0.5% at a 2-sided alpha of 0.05 without explicitly stating superiority or explicitly stating a test of zero difference / equality between arms (nor describing a non-superiority other test). Under Rule 6, `SUPERIORITY_OR_OTHER` without explicit disambiguating text must be coded as `not_stated`.

decisions.rationale: The measure description states that LS means were calculated using a 'restricted maximum likelihood (REML) based mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM)'. Per the Coding Sheet Rules (which give 'Mixed Model for Repeated Measures' / 'MMRM' as the example method name), 'mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM)' (reading_1) is the exact verbatim substring naming the missing-data method itself, whereas 'restricted maximum likelihood (REML) based' specifies the estimation criterion modifier.

Currently treated with IGlar (Insulin Glargine) and up to 3 oral antidiabetic drugs (OADs) (metformin, DPP-4 inhibitor, sulphonylurea/glinide or alpha-glucosidase inhibitor).

comparator_class_quotes.text: Insulin degludec/insulin aspart (IDegAsp) was injected subcutaneously (s.c.) in either abdomen, upper arm (deltoid area) or thigh. A pre-filled pen injector (PDS290) was used to administer IDegAsp. During treatment period subjects were allowed to continue up to 3 (oral antidiabetic drugs) OADs, except insulin glargine, sulphonylurea and glinides. In the IDegAsp twice daily (BID) simple titration algorithm arm, self-titration was performed twice weekly at intervals of 3-4 days and based upon a single pre-breakfast and pre-dinner self-measured plasma glucose (SMPG) value.

IDegAsp was injected subcutaneously (s.c.) in either abdomen, upper arm (deltoid area) or thigh. A pre-filled pen injector (PDS290) was used to administer IDegAsp. During treatment period subjects were allowed to continue up to 3 (oral antidiabetic drugs) OADs, except insulin glargine, sulphonylurea and glinides. In the IDegAsp twice daily (BID) stepwise titration algorithm arm, self-titration was done once weekly based on the lowest of 3 pre-breakfast and 3 pre-dinner SMPG values (measurements on 3 consecutive days prior to titration).

deciding_quotes.text: Omarigliptin will be considered non-inferior to sitagliptin if the upper bound of the two-sided 95% confidence interval of the between-treatment difference in least squares means for change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24 (omarigliptin minus sitagliptin) is not more than 0.3% (non-inferiority margin).

decisions.rationale: In analyses[2].nonInferiorityComment, 'not more than' is the relational condition on the upper bound of the 95% confidence interval ('the upper bound ... is not more than 0.3% (non-inferiority margin)'), whereas '0.3% (non-inferiority margin)' is the exact verbatim substring stating the non-inferiority margin itself per Section 6.

Participants received double blind albiglutide 30 mg as a subcutaneous injection weekly to Week 52.

Participants received double-blind albiglutide 30 mg as a subcutaneous injection weekly until Week 4. Starting at Week 4, participants received albiglutide 50 mg as a subcutaneous injection weekly to Week 52.

Participants received open-label liraglutide as a subcutaneous injection daily at a dose of 0.3 mg with weekly forced uptitrations to a dose of 0.6 mg then a dose of 0.9 mg (maximum dose in Japan). The dose of 0.9 mg daily was given to Week 52.

deciding_quotes.text: mixed model repeated measures (MMRM)

decisions.rationale: outcomeMeasures[0].description literally names 'mixed model repeated measures (MMRM)' as the longitudinal model used in the statistical analysis (with REML being the estimator modifier, while 'observed cases (OC)' in populationDescription is explicitly defined there as setting values measured after antidiabetic rescue medication to missing while all 150 FAS participants are analysed). reading_1 captures the exact concise verbatim substring naming the missing-data method per Rule 4.

deciding_quotes.text: Patients were orally administered Placebo matching empagliflozin 10 mg or 25 mg (1 tablet once daily, morning)
Patients were orally administered Empagliflozin 10 mg or 25mg (1 tablet once daily, morning over a period of 24 weeks)

on diet and exercise regimen who are EITHER drug-naïve (defined as absence of any oral antidiabetic therapy, glucagon like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analog or insulin for 12 weeks, 16 weeks for pioglitazone prior to randomisation) OR pre-treated with stable dose of
Treatment has to be unchanged for a minimum of 12 weeks prior to randomization.

decisions.rationale: Neither outcomeMeasures[0].groups[] nor armGroups[] mentions any continuing background antidiabetic therapy or diet and exercise regimen. eligibilityCriteria only describes pre-randomisation status (patients who are either drug-naïve or pre-treated with stable doses unchanged for a minimum of 12 weeks prior to randomization, and analyses[0].groupDescription similarly refers only to 'pre-treatment with metformin'), without stating that pre-randomisation antidiabetic therapy continues across the 24-week treatment period; diet and exercise also appears only in eligibilityCriteria rather than as a continuing background regimen in arm descriptions. Per Rule 5 and no-inference rules, 'not_stated' (reading_1) is correct.

decisions.rationale: From outcomeMeasures[0].groups[0..3].description, patients were randomized to investigational fixed-dose combination (FDC) tablets of empagliflozin (10 mg or 25 mg) and linagliptin 5 mg plus double-dummy matching placebo of empagliflozin versus active empagliflozin (10 mg or 25 mg) tablets plus double-dummy matching placebo of the FDC tablet. Per Rule 5, comparing an investigational combination against a different active drug/regimen where matching placebo tablets are double-dummy blinding inside active-drug arms (with no placebo-only control arm or identical unrandomized continuing background therapy across arms) is 'active_drug' (reading_2).

decisions.rationale: Prior oral antidiabetic drugs were discontinued at Visit 1 (eligibilityCriteria), open-label empagliflozin was administered during the preceding 16-week stabilisation period rather than as continuing background therapy, and during the double-blind treatment period empagliflozin was part of the randomized study regimens themselves (FDC tablet vs single-agent empagliflozin tablet with double-dummy placebos). No continuing background antidiabetic therapy (nor continuing diet and exercise in arm descriptions) is stated across the treatment period, so 'not_stated' (reading_2) applies.

measure.background_therapy_as_posted:
Stable daily dose(s) within 90 days prior to the day of screening of any of the following treatment regimens:
* 1-2 of the following oral anti-diabetic drugs:
* Metformin equal or above 1500 mg or maximum tolerated dose documented in the subject medical record),
* Sulfonylurea (equal or above half of the maximum approved dose according to local label or maximum tolerated dose as documented in subject medical record)
* Basal insulin alone (20% change in total daily dose of insulin glargine, insulin detemir, insulin degludec or NPH insulin) or
* Metformin (equal or above 1500 mg or maximum tolerated dose documented in the subject medical record) in combination with basal insulin (20% change in total daily dose of insulin glargine, insulin detemir, insulin degludec or NPH insulin)

decisions.rationale: In analyses[0].groupDescription, the missing-data handling procedure is not generic multiple imputation alone: it specifies separate-arm multiple imputation across 1000 complete imputed data sets plus a 0.4% penalty added to Week 26 values for prematurely discontinued subjects and subjects with missing Week 26 HbA1c values in the IDegAsp arm. reading_1 captures the complete verbatim missing-data method description while excluding the final ANCOVA sentence, whereas reading_2 omits the arm-specific 0.4% penalty imputation component.

deciding_quotes.text: Non-inferiority of IDegAsp OD versus IGlar OD + IAsp OD was considered confirmed if the 95% confidence interval for the mean treatment difference was entirely below 0.40%.

decisions.rationale: analyses[0].nonInferiorityComment does not use the word 'margin' and instead states the non-inferiority confirmation criterion via a directional confidence-interval bound ('entirely below 0.40%'). reading_1 copies the exact verbatim statement from nonInferiorityComment, preserving both the bound value (0.40%) and its stated direction and comparison context without inference.
